newsitem.title: INDIA: India court extends custody in arms drop case.
newsitem.headline: India court extends custody in arms drop case.

text.p: An Indian court on Friday extended judicial custody for five Latvians and a Briton accused of dropping weapons by parachute into a remote eastern region of India last year.
The court in the eastern city of Calcutta remanded former British army officer Peter Bleach, 44, and the five Latvians in judicial custody until December 6.
The accused, charged with sedition and conspiracy, were arrested last December 22, five days after a Russian AN-26 aircraft dropped the arms in West Bengal state.
Sedition carries a maximum penalty of death by hanging in India.
Authorities said they recovered 224 AK-47 and AK-56 rifles with more than 17,000 rounds of ammunition, eight rocket launchers, 80 anti-tank grenades and seven 9mm pistols.
The authorities believe the weapons were destined for the Hindu religious cult Ananda Marg, with headquarters close to the site of the drop.
The crew later flew to Phuket island in Thailand and Madras before being forced by Indian Air Force fighters to land in Bombay on December 22.
Bleach, who diplomats said served with the British army in Northern Ireland, has claimed he was acting as the "inside man" for the British government in the drop. Britain denies this.

Diplomats have said Britain tipped off India before the arms drop, and Home (Interior) Secretary Michael Howard said in January his government had supplied information to Indian authorities, which helped them to arrest Bleach and the others.
